name: Present perfect: experience, ever/never, just/already/yet
summary: Present Perfect zamoni o'tmishda sodir bo'lgan, ammo hozirgi paytda ham muhim yoki ta'sirga ega bo'lgan harakatlarni bildiradi.

usage.text: Hayotdagi tajribalar haqida gapirishda (qachon sodir bo'lgani muhim emas).

example.en: I have visited London three times.

usage.text: 'Ever' so'zi savollarda 'hech qachon' degan ma'noni bildiradi.

example.en: Have you ever eaten sushi?
example.uz: Siz hech qachon sushi yeb ko'rganmisiz?

usage.text: 'Never' so'zi darak gaplarda inkor ma'nosini beradi.

example.en: She has never flown in a plane.

usage.text: 'Just' yaqindagina sodir bo'lgan voqealar uchun ishlatiladi.

example.en: I have just finished my homework.

usage.text: 'Already' allaqachon bajarilgan ishni, 'yet' esa hali bajarilmagan ishni bildiradi.

example.en: He has already left, but they haven't arrived yet.
example.uz: U allaqachon ketdi, lekin ular hali kelishmadi.

example.en: I have seen that film.
She hasn't finished yet.
Have you ever been to Paris?

structure.formula: Yes, subject + have/has. / No, subject + haven't/hasn't.

example.en: Yes, I have. / No, she hasn't.

tip: Eslab qoling: 'He/She/It' olmoshlari bilan 'has', qolganlari bilan 'have' ishlatiladi va fe'lning uchinchi shakli (V3) qo'shiladi.

name: for / since, How long
summary: Bu qoida o'tmishda boshlanib, hozirgacha davom etayotgan harakatlarning davomiyligini ko'rsatish uchun ishlatiladi.

usage.text: 'For' vaqt davomiyligini (qancha vaqt?) ko'rsatish uchun ishlatiladi.

example.en: I have lived here for three years.
example.uz: Men bu yerda uch yildan beri yashayman.

usage.text: 'Since' ish boshlangan aniq vaqtni (qachondan beri?) ko'rsatadi.

example.en: She has worked here since 2020.

usage.text: 'How long' davomiylik haqida savol berish uchun ishlatiladi.

example.en: How long have you known him?
We have studied English for two hours.
example.uz: Biz ikki soatdan beri ingliz tilini o'rganmoqdamiz.

example.en: I haven't seen him since Monday.
example.uz: Men uni dushanba kunidan beri ko'rmadim.

example.en: How long have you lived in this city?

structure.formula: For + time period / Since + point in time

example.en: For five years. / Since May.
example.uz: Besh yildan beri. / May oyidan beri.

tip: 'For' so'zidan keyin vaqt oralig'i (three days, two years), 'since' dan keyin esa aniq boshlanish nuqtasi (Monday, 10 o'clock) kelishini unutmang!

name: Present perfect vs past simple; been vs gone
name_uz: Present Perfect va Past Simple; been va gone
summary: Past Simple aniq o'tmish vaqti uchun, Present Perfect esa hozirgi natija yoki tajriba uchun ishlatiladi. 'Been' borgan-kelgan, 'gone' esa ketgan va hali qaytmagan ma'noni beradi.

usage.text: Past Simple aniq o'tmish payti (yesterday, in 2010) ko'rsatilganda ishlatiladi.

example.en: I visited Rome last year.

usage.text: Present Perfect esa vaqt ko'rsatilmaganda va natija muhim bo'lganda ishlatiladi.

example.en: I have visited Rome.

usage.text: 'Have/has been' - biror joyga borib qaytib kelganini bildiradi.

example.en: She has been to the shop. (She is back now)
example.uz: U do'konga borib keldi. (Hozir u qaytgan)

usage.text: 'Have/has gone' - biror joyga ketgan va hali qaytib kelmaganini bildiradi.

example.en: He has gone to the shop. (He is still there or on the way)

structure.formula: Subject + V2 (Past Simple) vs Subject + have/has + V3 (Present Perfect)

example.en: I bought a car yesterday. / I have bought a new car.
example.uz: Men kecha mashina sotib oldim. / Men yangi mashina sotib oldim.

structure.formula: Subject + didn't + V1 vs Subject + haven't/hasn't + V3

example.en: I didn't see him. / I haven't seen him.
example.uz: Men uni ko'rmadim. / Men uni ko'rmaganman.

structure.formula: Did + subject + V1? vs Have/Has + subject + V3?

example.en: Did you go? / Have you been?

structure.formula: Yes, I did. / Yes, I have.

example.en: Yes, I did. / Yes, I have.

tip: Gapda 'yesterday' yoki 'last year' kabi aniq o'tmish vaqti bo'lsa, hech qachon Present Perfect ishlatmang — faqat Past Simple ishlating!
